summary: Go TaskUpdate matches the public name, most visible input fields, persistent task storage, basic field mutation, deletion cleanup, dependency edge mutation, and the model-facing happy-path text. It is not exact parity with the TS baseline. The largest remaining gaps are task-v2 exposure gating, strict input/presence semantics, structured output data, TaskCompleted hook blocking, teammate owner/mailbox lifecycle, app-state/update notifications, verification-nudge gating, Go-only dependency/status behavior, tool metadata, and parity test coverage.

gaps.title: TaskUpdate is registered unconditionally instead of following the TS todo-v2 gate
gaps.description: TS exposes TaskUpdate only when todo-v2 is enabled. CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS force-enables todo-v2, otherwise interactive sessions enable it and non-interactive sessions hide task-v2 tools. Go has an equivalent RuntimeScope.IsTodoV2Enabled helper, but SetupRegistry registers TaskUpdate and the other task-v2 tools unconditionally.

ts_evidence.note: isTodoV2Enabled returns true for CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS or interactive sessions.
TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, and TaskList are added only when isTodoV2Enabled() is true.
TaskUpdateTool.isEnabled() delegates to isTodoV2Enabled().

go_evidence.note: Go already has RuntimeScope.IsTodoV2Enabled with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS plus interactive semantics.
SetupRegistry registers TaskCreate, TaskList, TaskUpdate, and TaskGet without checking RuntimeScope.IsTodoV2Enabled().
TaskUpdate and TodoWrite both have deferred discovery metadata, so unconditional registration can still expose both systems through ToolSearch.

gaps.impact: Go can advertise and execute TaskUpdate in modes where TS would not expose it, changing planning behavior and task-vs-todo state ownership.

gaps.title: Go does not enforce TS strict-object and field-presence semantics
gaps.description: TS uses z.strictObject and distinguishes a missing optional string from a present empty string with undefined checks. Go publishes a similar visible schema, but parseInput uses json.Unmarshal into TaskUpdateInput, which ignores unknown keys, accepts a hidden id alias, trims taskId, and stores optional strings as plain strings so empty subject/description/activeForm/owner cannot be set. Empty status is treated as absent instead of a schema error.

ts_evidence.note: The input schema is z.strictObject with taskId plus optional subject, description, activeForm, status, addBlocks, addBlockedBy, owner, and metadata.
TS applies string field updates when the field is present, even if the new value is an empty string.
Status is handled only when provided through the validated schema; an empty string is not a valid status enum value.

go_evidence.note: TaskUpdateInput includes a hidden ID alias and uses plain string fields for optional string parameters.
The published schema lists taskId and visible optional fields but cannot express strict additionalProperties:false.
Execute trims taskId, falls back to id, and errors when the trimmed value is empty.
Status validation is skipped when in.Status is an empty string.
Go only updates optional strings when their value is non-empty, so present empty strings are dropped.

gaps.impact: TS-invalid inputs can succeed in Go, and TS-valid clearing updates can become no-ops. This breaks replay parity and hides model/schema drift.

gaps.title: Structured TaskUpdate output data and statusChange are missing
gaps.description: TS TaskUpdate returns typed data with success, taskId, updatedFields, error, statusChange, and verificationNudgeNeeded, then maps it to a non-error tool_result string. Go TaskUpdate returns plain text directly through ToolResult.Content and loses structured fields such as statusChange and verificationNudgeNeeded. Go error paths also mix non-error text with IsError=true business errors rather than preserving the TS success:false data contract.

ts_evidence.note: TS declares an output schema with success, taskId, updatedFields, error, statusChange, and verificationNudgeNeeded.
Not-found returns structured success:false data.
Successful updates return structured data including statusChange and verificationNudgeNeeded.
mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam renders content while keeping failure results non-error.

go_evidence.note: Go ToolResult primarily exposes Content string, ContentBlocks, IsError, NewMessages, and string Metadata, with no TaskUpdate typed data field.
The registry converts ToolResult directly into a ToolResultBlock, copying only Content, blocks, IsError, messages, and metadata.
Not-found returns plain text 'Task not found'.
Deletion returns plain text and does not expose a structured statusChange.
Successful updates render text directly and append the verification nudge to the content.

gaps.impact: Callers cannot inspect the same output data TS provides, parity fixtures cannot compare typed results, and tool-result error semantics diverge.

gaps.title: TaskCompleted hooks are not executed before completing a task
gaps.description: TS runs TaskCompleted hooks before applying status=completed. Blocking hook feedback prevents the update and returns success:false with formatted TaskCompleted feedback. Go's hooks package can load and run HookTaskCompleted, but TaskUpdateTool has no HookRunner field, registry setup does not retain or inject a TaskUpdateTool hook runner, and Execute updates status directly without hook execution.

ts_evidence.note: TaskUpdate calls executeTaskCompletedHooks before setting updates.status and returns blocking errors without mutating the task.
executeTaskCompletedHooks builds a TaskCompleted hook payload with task id, subject, description, teammate name, and team name.
Blocking feedback is formatted as TaskCompleted hook feedback.

go_evidence.note: Go defines HookTaskCompleted.
HookInput already has task_id, task_subject, task_description, teammate_name, and team_name fields.
TaskUpdateTool only stores TaskStore; unlike TaskCreateTool, it has no HookRunner field.
Status updates are placed into updates and persisted without TaskCompleted hook execution.
TaskUpdateTool is constructed and registered without retention or hook-runner injection.
Runtime hook runner is assigned to AgentTool and TeamManager, not TaskUpdateTool.
Session switching updates AgentTool and TeamManager hook runners, not TaskUpdateTool.

gaps.impact: A TS hook that blocks incomplete or unsafe task completion is bypassed in Go, so task state can become completed when TS would stop the transition.

gaps.title: Teammate owner assignment, mailbox notification, and completion reminder are missing
gaps.description: TS auto-assigns the current agent as owner when a swarm teammate starts an unowned task, sends a task_assignment mailbox message when owner changes, and appends a TaskList reminder when a teammate completes a task. Go only applies an explicit owner string and has no TaskUpdate path to current agent name, team name, teammate color, mailbox delivery, or teammate completion reminder.

ts_evidence.note: When agent swarms are enabled, status=in_progress and owner is omitted, TS sets owner to getAgentName() if the task had no owner.
When owner changes under agent swarms, TS writes a task_assignment JSON message to the owner's mailbox.
Task assignment mailbox messages have a typed task_assignment envelope.
A teammate completing a task receives a reminder to call TaskList.

go_evidence.note: TaskUpdate only updates owner when a non-empty owner is explicitly provided; there is no auto-owner branch.
The final response only includes updated fields, verification nudge, and rejected-edge warning; no teammate TaskList reminder is appended.
Go has a mailbox send path in SendMessageTool, but TaskUpdate does not call it.
The structured-protocol classifier list does not include task_assignment, so mailbox task assignment handling is not wired through this path either.

gaps.impact: Team task handoff and worker guidance differ from TS. Teammates may not be notified of assignments and may not be nudged to pick the next unblocked task.

gaps.title: TaskUpdate does not mirror TS app-state expansion or task-update notifications
gaps.description: TS TaskUpdate auto-expands the task view and the underlying task utilities notify in-process subscribers after task mutations. Go's Tool.Execute signature has no ToolUseContext or setAppState channel, TaskUpdate ignores context, and TaskStore update/delete/block operations mutate files without a task-updated signal.

ts_evidence.note: TaskUpdate sets appState.expandedView to 'tasks' when called.
TS exposes onTasksUpdated and wraps notifyTasksUpdated so listener failures do not affect mutations.
updateTaskUnsafe writes the task and calls notifyTasksUpdated().
deleteTask removes references, notifies subscribers, and returns success.

go_evidence.note: Go tools receive only context.Context and input map; no app-state setter is available at the tool boundary.
updateDetailed writes the task and optional dependent updates but does not emit a task-updated signal.
delete removes task files and dependency references without notifying an observer.
blockTask mutates dependency edges without notifying an observer.
Go has a TUI AppState type, but TaskUpdate is not connected to it.

gaps.impact: Interactive UI/task panels and in-process listeners cannot react with TS-equivalent immediacy, and TaskUpdate cannot force the tasks view open.

gaps.title: Verification nudge fires without TS feature, GrowthBook, and main-thread gates
gaps.description: TS only computes verificationNudgeNeeded when VERIFICATION_AGENT is enabled, GrowthBook key tengu_hive_evidence is true, the caller is not a subagent, and this update changed status to completed. The boolean is part of structured output and only the mapper appends text. Go computes and appends the nudge whenever the input status is completed and all tasks are completed, regardless of feature flags, GrowthBook, current agent id, or whether status actually changed.

ts_evidence.note: TS gates verificationNudgeNeeded on feature('VERIFICATION_AGENT'), GrowthBook tengu_hive_evidence, !context.agentId, and updates.status === 'completed'.
The nudge is returned as a boolean in structured output.
The result mapper appends the note only when verificationNudgeNeeded is true.

go_evidence.note: taskVerificationNudgeNeeded checks only task count, all-completed status, and subject text.
TaskUpdate calls taskVerificationNudgeNeeded whenever input status is completed.
Go renders the nudge text directly.
The test asserts the nudge appears without setting feature flags, GrowthBook state, or agent context.

gaps.impact: Go can ask for verification in sessions where TS would stay quiet, including subagent/team contexts and feature-disabled environments.

gaps.title: Go adds dependency/status behaviors that TS TaskUpdate does not implement
gaps.description: Go prevents in_progress when blockers remain, refuses self/cyclic dependency edges and reports warnings, and removes dependency references when a task is completed. TS TaskUpdate does not check blockers before status=in_progress, blockTask only fails for missing endpoints, and completing a task leaves dependency edges in the store. Some of the Go behavior may be useful, but it is not exact parity.

ts_evidence.note: TS regular status updates only run completion hooks for completed, then assign updates.status when status differs.
TS blockTask checks both tasks exist and adds edges; it does not detect cycles or self-edges.
TS updateTask applies partial updates and does not remove dependencies when status becomes completed.
TS dependency-reference cleanup is attached to deleteTask, not completion.

go_evidence.note: Go blocks status=in_progress while non-completed/non-deleted blockers remain.
Go blockTask rejects self/missing/cyclic edges.
Go implements transitive cycle detection.
Go removes dependency references when status changes to completed.
Go reports rejected edge warnings in the tool result.
A Go test locks the cycle-refusal behavior.

gaps.impact: Go can reject or rewrite task graphs that TS would allow, and task dependency state can diverge after completion.

gaps.title: TaskUpdate operates on unvalidated Go task rows and a wider persisted shape
gaps.description: TS getTask migrates legacy ant statuses, validates against TaskSchema, and returns null for invalid rows before TaskUpdate mutates them. Go reads JSON directly into TaskItem with Status as a free string and extra persisted fields such as comments and timestamps. TaskUpdate can therefore operate on rows TS would ignore or normalize, and the on-disk shape is not TS-compatible.

ts_evidence.note: TS TaskSchema restricts status to pending/in_progress/completed and defines the task fields consumed by tools.
getTask migrates old statuses for ant users and safeParse-validates before returning a task.
listTasks loads rows through getTask and filters null invalid rows.

go_evidence.note: Go TaskItem includes status as an unconstrained string plus comments and timestamp fields.
TaskStore.get unmarshals directly and returns the row without schema validation or status migration.
updateDetailed mutates whichever row readTaskLocked returns.
readTaskLocked unmarshals directly into TaskItem and accepts any status string.

gaps.impact: Corrupt, legacy, or Go-only task rows can be updated in Go when TS would skip them, and persisted files can drift away from TS task schema expectations.

gaps.title: TaskUpdate lacks TS tool metadata hooks beyond registry-level deferred discovery
gaps.description: TS TaskUpdate declares searchHint, maxResultSizeChars, prompt, outputSchema, userFacingName, shouldDefer, isConcurrencySafe, toAutoClassifierInput, and renderToolUseMessage. Go has registry-level deferred/search metadata for TaskUpdate and a short Description, but TaskUpdateTool itself has no concurrency-safe marker, output schema, prompt equivalent, user-facing name, max-result size, render hook, or auto-classifier input.

ts_evidence.note: TS declares the metadata and behavioral hooks on the tool definition.
TS provides a detailed prompt covering update usage, deletion, dependencies, status workflow, staleness, and examples.

go_evidence.note: Go has a registry metadata mechanism for ShouldDefer, AlwaysLoad, and SearchHint only.
TaskUpdate gets deferred metadata through the builtin table, with a different search hint.
TaskUpdateTool defines Store, Name, Description, Schema, and Execute; no IsConcurrentSafe or classifier/prompt/output-schema methods are present.
The Go loop uses an optional IsConcurrentSafe interface for concurrency scheduling.

gaps.impact: Go may serialize independent TaskUpdate calls that TS marks concurrency-safe, cannot provide the same classifier text, and cannot surface the same rich prompt/output metadata.

gaps.title: TaskUpdate parity tests cover only happy-path text, deletion cleanup, and unconditional nudge
gaps.description: The existing Go tests exercise a basic update with owner and blockedBy, deletion dependency cleanup, cycle refusal at store level, and the unconditional verification nudge. They do not cover TS parity for enablement gating, strict unknown-key rejection, present-empty-string updates, hidden id alias rejection, structured output/statusChange, TaskCompleted blocking hooks, mailbox assignment, teammate auto-owner, app-state/task notifications, TS feature-gated verification nudge, or Go-only dependency behavior decisions.

ts_evidence.note: Strict input and field set are defined in TS.
Structured output contract is defined in TS.
TS teammate auto-owner and mailbox side effects are implemented.
TS TaskCompleted hook blocking behavior is implemented.
TS verification-nudge gates are implemented.

go_evidence.note: Current TaskUpdate test covers a basic in_progress owner plus addBlockedBy flow and string output.
Current deletion test covers dependency cleanup after deleted.
Current nudge test asserts unconditional nudge text.
Cycle refusal is tested only at TaskStore.blockTask level.
Hook tests are for TaskCreate, and the blocking hook test is skipped; there is no TaskUpdate TaskCompleted hook test.

gaps.impact: Future changes can claim TaskUpdate parity while missing the main runtime and lifecycle behaviors that make the TS tool different from a plain text mutation helper.

candidate_tasks.title: Gate TaskUpdate registration with todo-v2 enablement
candidate_tasks.objective: Register TaskUpdate only under the same todo-v2 rules as TS, and keep TaskUpdate hidden in non-interactive sessions unless CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS is truthy.
acceptance: Interactive registries expose TaskUpdate.
Non-interactive registries without CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS do not expose TaskUpdate.
Non-interactive registries with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS truthy expose TaskUpdate.
TodoWrite/task-v2 mutual exposure matches the broader task-tool policy chosen for TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskList.

candidate_tasks.title: Implement strict TaskUpdate input and presence-aware optional fields
candidate_tasks.objective: Match TS z.strictObject validation and optional-field presence semantics for TaskUpdate input.
acceptance: Unknown top-level keys are rejected for TaskUpdate.
The hidden id alias is no longer accepted unless explicitly documented as a deliberate compatibility extension.
taskId is validated as a required string without trim-based reinterpretation.
Present empty subject, description, activeForm, and owner values update the stored task.
Empty status is rejected as invalid instead of treated as omitted.
metadata null values still delete keys.

candidate_tasks.title: Add TS-compatible structured TaskUpdate result data
candidate_tasks.objective: Expose TaskUpdate result data equivalent to TS outputSchema while preserving model-facing rendered text.
acceptance: TaskUpdate success data includes success, taskId, updatedFields, optional statusChange, and verificationNudgeNeeded.
TaskUpdate failure data includes success:false, taskId, updatedFields:[], and error.
Not-found and hook-blocked failures render as non-error tool_result content like TS.
Deletion reports updatedFields:['deleted'] and statusChange from previous status to deleted.
Verification nudge text is produced by result mapping from a boolean, not by mutating the primary data shape.

candidate_tasks.title: Wire TaskCompleted hooks into TaskUpdate
candidate_tasks.objective: Run TaskCompleted hooks before status=completed is persisted and block the transition when hooks block, matching TS.
acceptance: TaskUpdateTool has a HookRunner or equivalent hook access path.
Startup and session switching inject the active HookRunner into the registered TaskUpdateTool.
status=completed invokes HookTaskCompleted with task_id, task_subject, task_description, teammate_name, and team_name before mutation.
Blocking hook output prevents status change and returns formatted TaskCompleted feedback.
Abort/cancellation context is honored for hook execution.

candidate_tasks.title: Implement teammate owner and mailbox side effects for TaskUpdate
candidate_tasks.objective: Mirror TS swarm-aware TaskUpdate behavior for auto-owner assignment, task_assignment mailbox delivery, and teammate completion reminders.
acceptance: When agent teams are enabled, status=in_progress with omitted owner and an unowned task sets owner to the current agent name.
Changing owner under agent teams writes a task_assignment JSON envelope to the assignee mailbox with taskId, subject, description, assignedBy, and timestamp.
Mailbox sender name and color or the nearest Go equivalent are populated consistently.
When a teammate marks a task completed, the rendered result includes the TS TaskList reminder.
No mailbox side effect occurs outside agent-team mode.

candidate_tasks.title: Add TaskUpdate app-state and task-update notification lifecycle
candidate_tasks.objective: Provide a Go runtime path for TaskUpdate to notify UI/listeners and expand the task view in interactive mode, or document and encode an explicit non-UI divergence.
acceptance: Task mutations emit a task-updated signal after update, delete, and dependency edge changes.
Listener failures do not fail the task mutation.
Interactive TaskUpdate can request or perform task-view expansion equivalent to TS expandedView='tasks'.
Non-interactive callers remain unaffected.
If exact AppState parity is out of scope, the divergence is represented by a tested no-op contract rather than accidental absence.

candidate_tasks.title: Match TS verification-nudge gating
candidate_tasks.objective: Gate TaskUpdate verification nudges on the same feature, experiment, main-thread, and actual-status-change conditions as TS.
acceptance: No nudge appears unless the Go equivalent of VERIFICATION_AGENT and tengu_hive_evidence are enabled.
No nudge appears when the current context is a subagent/agent-owned context.
No nudge appears when input status=completed but the persisted task was already completed.
Nudge appears when the final main-thread completion closes 3+ non-verification tasks under enabled gates.
The structured result carries verificationNudgeNeeded separately from rendered text.

candidate_tasks.title: Resolve Go-only dependency and blocked-status semantics
candidate_tasks.objective: Bring TaskUpdate dependency/status behavior into exact TS parity or encode intentional divergences behind explicit compatibility decisions and tests.
acceptance: status=in_progress behavior for tasks with open blockers matches TS or is explicitly gated as a deliberate Go extension.
Dependency edge creation accepts/rejects self and cyclic edges according to the chosen parity policy.
Completion does not remove dependency references if exact TS parity is selected.
Deletion cleanup continues to remove references, matching TS deleteTask.
Rendered result and structured result do not surface Go-only warnings unless that divergence is intentionally retained.

candidate_tasks.title: Validate and normalize task rows before TaskUpdate mutation
candidate_tasks.objective: Make TaskStore.get/readTaskLocked apply TS-compatible task schema validation and legacy status migration before TaskUpdate mutates a row.
acceptance: TaskUpdate treats invalid task rows as not found, matching TS getTask returning null.
Legacy statuses open/resolved/planning/implementing/reviewing/verifying normalize under the same conditions as TS or a documented Go compatibility policy.
Persisted task shape used by task-v2 tools is TS-compatible or extra fields are isolated from TS parity paths.
TaskUpdate cannot mutate rows with statuses outside pending/in_progress/completed unless status=deleted is the requested pseudo-action.

candidate_tasks.title: Expose TaskUpdate tool metadata parity
candidate_tasks.objective: Add the TaskUpdate-specific metadata surfaces TS exposes: concurrency safety, prompt, output schema, user-facing name, max result size, render behavior, and auto-classifier input.
acceptance: TaskUpdate implements IsConcurrentSafe() true or equivalent scheduler metadata.
TaskUpdate exposes userFacingName='TaskUpdate' where Go has a user-facing metadata surface.
TaskUpdate prompt content covers TS usage guidance, deletion, dependencies, status workflow, staleness, and examples.
TaskUpdate searchHint matches or intentionally maps from TS 'update a task'.
TaskUpdate auto-classifier input joins taskId, status when present, and subject when present.
TaskUpdate max-result/output-schema metadata is available to the same consumers as other structured Go tools.

candidate_tasks.title: Add focused TaskUpdate parity regression tests
candidate_tasks.objective: Create a regression suite that locks TaskUpdate parity for strict input, output data, hooks, teammate lifecycle, notification lifecycle, verification gating, and dependency decisions.
acceptance: Tests fail against the current implementation for known TaskUpdate gaps and pass after the corresponding tasks land.

Coverage includes strict unknown-key rejection, present-empty-string updates, hidden id alias policy, structured statusChange, not-found non-error data, deleted pseudo-status, TaskCompleted blocking hook rollback, mailbox assignment, auto-owner, teammate completion reminder, task-update notification, verification gates, and dependency policy.
Skipped tests, if any, name the exact blocking task id and acceptance condition for unskip.
The suite is isolated from global CLAUDE_HOME, CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID, team env, and feature flags.
